body:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Jan 24, 2025 at 9:12 AM PST
Subject: Rate card source + update cadence (GPU hourly costs) for Unit Economics dashboard

Laura — quick clarification needed for PM-483 / unit economics dashboard.

We’re wiring the hourly aggregation job to a “GPU hourly cost rate card” table. Before Engineering bakes assumptions into the pipeline, can you confirm:

1) Source of truth: is the rate card derived from invoices (AWS/GCP/Azure) or from forecasted assumptions (FP&A model)?
2) Update cadence: monthly vs quarterly? and do we ever back-edit a past period?
3) Versioning: do we expect a stable version pinned per reporting period (e.g., QTD views don’t shift when rates update)?

Engineering is asking what to display in the dashboard UI (rate card “as of” + version) and how to handle mid-quarter changes.

If you have a short written policy, that would be ideal.

Thanks,
Rishi
—
Rishi Malhotra
FP&A | Redwood Inference



From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Jan 24, 2025 at 10:03 AM PST
Subject: Re: Rate card source + update cadence (GPU hourly costs) for Unit Economics dashboard

Rishi — yes, we should document this explicitly. Here’s the policy I want Engineering to implement (aligned with how we report infra cost in FP&A):

1) Source of truth / provenance
- The rate card is Finance-owned and lives in the Finance shared drive (same file Engineering is referencing: “gpu-cost-rate-card-2025q4”).
- Inputs are ultimately invoice/billing based where possible:
  - Public cloud: AWS CUR / GCP billing export (effective blended $/GPU-hour by region + instance family), net of committed use discounts as amortized in the month.
  - Colos / private fleet: vendor invoices + internal depreciation schedule (allocated to regions where hardware is deployed).
- Where we don’t have a clean invoice breakout by GPU SKU/region (e.g., shared invoices), we use an allocation rule documented in the methodology note.

2) Update cadence
- “Published” rate cards update quarterly for reporting stability (Q1/Q2/Q3/Q4).
- Mid-quarter we may maintain a “draft / provisional” sheet for planning, but we should not change the published version used for exec reporting.

3) Versioning and back-edits
- No in-place edits to a published period.
- If a correction is required (e.g., billing true-up), create a new version with an incremented suffix (e.g., 2025Q4.v2), and explicitly label the reason in a changelog.
- Dashboard must show: (a) rate_card_period (e.g., 2025Q4), (b) rate_card_version (v1/v2), and (c) published_at timestamp.
- For standard Finance reporting views, default to the latest PUBLISHED version for the selected period.

Attaching a lightweight changelog template we can start using.

Laura
—
Laura Bennett
CFO | Redwood Inference

Attachment: rate-card-change-log.md (text)



From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Fri, Jan 24, 2025 at 10:21 AM PST
Subject: Re: Rate card source + update cadence (GPU hourly costs) for Unit Economics dashboard

+1 to quarterly published + versioned corrections.

Logan — can we make sure the pipeline supports selecting a rate_card_version and that the default “finance” view pins to the published version? We’ve had issues in other dashboards where a “lookup table” is overwritten and historical time series shift.

Also, request: include “effective_start” and “effective_end” in the warehouse dimension table so we can reconstruct any report as-of a given date.

Dylan



From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: finops-support@cloudability.example
Date: Fri, Jan 24, 2025 at 12:07 PM PST
Subject: Re: Rate card source + update cadence (GPU hourly costs) for Unit Economics dashboard

Works for us.

Implementation plan (assuming Finance confirms):
- We’ll ingest the rate card into a warehouse table with:
  - rate_card_period (e.g., 2025Q4)
  - rate_card_version (v1, v2)
  - published_status (draft|published)
  - published_at
  - effective_start_utc / effective_end_utc
  - region_normalized, provider, capacity_type (on_demand|reserved|colo), gpu_family
  - gpu_hourly_cost_usd
- Aggregation job will join on region/provider/capacity_type/gpu_family + event hour.
- For “finance-aligned” metrics, queries will default to published_status=published and choose the max(published_at) within the selected period.
- For “live” troubleshooting views, we can expose draft (but behind internal flag).

Question for Laura/Rishi: is “period” defined as fiscal quarter only, or do you want a monthly versioned card as well for QTD reporting? We can support both, but would prefer to keep the number of versions small.

(Looping Cloudability support only because we’re validating the CUR export fields we can reliably map to gpu_family/region.)

Logan



From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Jan 24, 2025 at 3:46 PM PST
Subject: Re: Rate card source + update cadence (GPU hourly costs) for Unit Economics dashboard

Thanks all.

On the “period” question: for v1, let’s keep the published card quarterly. FP&A will still do QTD reporting off the quarter card (we’re not trying to be penny-precise month-to-month yet; stability > precision for exec KPI).

If we later see large within-quarter rate moves (e.g., reserved coverage changes materially), we can revisit and move to monthly published cards, but that should be a deliberate change with Finance sign-off.

Laura — confirming your direction: quarterly published, no in-place edits; corrections = new version (v2) + changelog. I’ll add this to the PM-483 sign-off checklist.

Rishi

Attachment referenced: gpu-cost-rate-card-2025q4.xlsx (Office Spreadsheet)
